articles.description: Iran's main oil-loading terminals have remained empty for weeks.

articles.title: North America Breaks Rig Count Addition Streak, BH Shows
articles.description: North America dropped five rigs week on week, according to Baker Hughes' latest North America rotary rig count.

articles.title: Philippines, USA Looking to Expand Cooperation on Energy Security
articles.description: The Philippines and the U.S. are exploring an expansion of collaboration on energy security, according to Manila's energy department.

articles.title: Vår Energi, Equinor find gas and condensate at Lakris prospect
articles.description: Vår Energi and its partner Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery at the Lakris prospect in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace in the Norwegian Sea.

articles.title: Brazil will drill: why a global transition leader is set on oil and gas expansion
articles.description: Brazil leads in clean energy but – whether Lula or Bolsonaro wins – the next government will charge ahead with oil and gas expansion.

articles.title: EIA Sees Smaller Oil Crunch in 2026
articles.description: The U.S. Energy Information Administration tightened its oil crunch prediction for 2026 in its latest short term energy outlook.

articles.title: Europa Oil & Gas secures 12-month EG-08 licence extension
articles.description: Europa Oil & Gas has been granted a 12-month extension to the first exploration sub-period of its offshore EG-08 block in Equatorial Guinea, moving the deadline from 4 October 2026 to 4 October 2027.

articles.title: NG Energy starts production at Aruchara-6 well in Colombia
articles.description: Canada-based gas producer NG Energy International (NGE) has brought the Aruchara-6 well into production at Maria Conchita Block, with drilling also under way at Sinú-9 block in Colombia.

articles.title: Trump Says Diesel Deal Aims to Keep Russia Talks Going
articles.description: President Donald Trump said he cut a diesel export deal with Russia and delayed imposing further sanctions because he doesn't want to drive Vladimir Putin away from peace talks.

articles.title: Wright Says Gas Prices Peaked As Brent Holds Above $108
articles.description: Brent crude futures briefly tagged $109.99 a barrel in overnight trading before retreating from five-month highs during the Asian session and into European trading, as signs of recovering Middle Eastern supply offset renewed attacks on energy infrastructure and critical maritime shipping lanes. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright reinforced expectations of easing fuel prices at the pump, with ABC News quoting him on Sunday as saying gasoline and diesel prices had "peaked." "Both gasoline and diesel prices peaked a few weeks ago," Wright said, adding…

articles.title: Venezuela Sees Nearly $76B Oil Investment Over 5 Years
articles.description: Venezuela expects almost $76 billion of investment in its oil and gas sector over the next five years, Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said Saturday.

articles.title: Mozambique Pitches Sasol and ROMPCO on $250 Million Gas Project
articles.description: Mozambique is in discussions with South African energy firm Sasol and pipeline company ROMPCO to potentially invest in a new $250 million gas project offshore Mozambique that could send more gas to South Africa. Mozambique plans to have floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) at the new project at the coastal town of Inhassoro and the port of Beira, as the country aims to become a “power hub” for the region, Rudêncio Morais, CEO and chairman of Mozambique’s national oil and gas company, Empresa Nacional de Hidrocarbonetos…

articles.title: Trump Defends Russia Sanctions Waiver as Rift With Ukraine Deepens
articles.description: President Donald Trump defended his decision to waive sweeping sanctions planned against Russia as an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table amid strong criticism from Kyiv and some US lawmakers that it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin. Trump signed an executive order late on October 16 that waives new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US senator Lindsey Graham, an ardent supporter of Ukraine, days after giving temporary relief on Russian diesel sanctions. Trump signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who want…

articles.title: Qatari LNG Cargo Heads Through Red Sea to Europe in Rare Suez Run
articles.description: A Qatari LNG cargo is traveling north in the Red Sea to deliver gas to Europe via the Suez Canal in a rare shipment on the shortest but dangerous route to Europe amid the Houthi threats to tankers in the southern Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The tanker loaded LNG from Qatar in August and is now moving north in the Red Sea with Poland as its destination, Bloomberg reported on Monday, quoting vessel-tracking data it had compiled. Qatar’s state firm QatarEnergy has a term contract with Polish energy group Orlen, as well as with other…

articles.title: Woodside pauses Scarborough gas unit after Greenpeace protest
articles.description: Woodside Energy has suspended activity at a floating production unit central to its $12.5bn Scarborough natural gas development following a protest by Greenpeace off Western Australia’s northwest coast, reported Reuters.

articles.title: China’s Solar Exports Keep Falling as Beijing Mulls Export Controls
articles.description: Chinese exports of solar power equipment extended their declining trend this year with a 6.4% drop in September from a year earlier, while China’s authorities consider export controls and/or bans on a dozen solar manufacturing technologies. The world’s top solar manufacturer shipped 1.21 million metric tons of solar cells and panels last month, according to customs data cited by Reuters. While the exports rose from August, they were over 6% lower compared to September last year, and contributed to a year-to-date slump of 9.5%…

articles.title: Woodside Resumes Work at Australian LNG Project after Greenpeace Stunt
articles.description: Australia’s Woodside Energy on Monday announced it had resumed work on the soon-to-be-commissioned Scarborough project offshore Western Australia, which is set to export LNG to global markets and supply gas to the domestic market. This weekend, two Greenpeace activists climbed onto the gas platform at the Scarborough Energy Project, forcing a pause in the commissioning work with their unauthorized boarding of the facility. After a weekend of standoff, the two protesters were safely removed from the facility and charged with interfering with…

articles.title: Japan’s Electricity Prices Surge 25% as LNG and Coal Costs Soar
articles.description: Japan’s average power prices jumped by over 25% at the start of this week from the previous week amid soaring LNG and higher coal prices. The nationwide power price rose by over 25% week-to-week to $0.19 (31.15 Japanese yen) per kilowatt-hour (kWh) on Monday, Bloomberg reported, citing data from Japan Electric Power Exchange. Japan, one of the world’s biggest LNG importers, this summer reduced gas-fired generation in favor of coal as the price of liquefied natural gas remained elevated. Japan has been burning more coal and less gas…

articles.title: China's Coal Production Slumps 6.8% as Winter Supply Fears Grow
articles.description: China’s coal production last month fell by 6.8% on the year to a total 385 million tons. The monthly total was, however, an increase on August, Bloomberg reported, citing the country’s statistics agency. China has been curbing coal production this year on abundant inventories and lower demand from power generators earlier in the year. In September, thermal power generation declined 1.4% year over year. With winter starting, however, the production—and power generation—trend could reverse as demand for heating peaks. Earlier…

articles.title: India's Crude Oil Import Bill Soars 46% as Middle East Crisis Drives Up Prices
articles.description: India paid $15.4 billion to import crude oil in September, up by 46% from the year-ago import bill of $10.5 billion, as international oil prices and the Indian import crude basket soared amid reignited tensions in the Middle East. India, the world’s third-largest crude oil importer, saw its crude imports rise by 7% in September from a year earlier. But the price to pay for crude oil imports soared by 46%, according to data from the Oil Ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) cited by the Times of India. The Indian basket…

articles.title: Greenpeace Protest Forces Shutdown at Woodside’s $12.5 Billion Gas Project
articles.description: Two Greenpeace activists were arrested in Australia after they caused a halt in operations at Woodside Energy’s Scarborough LNG platform, off the coast of Western Australia. The two were charged with “interfering with offshore petroleum installations or operations”, the local authorities said in a statement as cited by ABC. The maximum penalty for that charge is 10 years in prison. The two activists boarded the platform on Saturday and spent the night there, Reuters reported, citing a Greenpeace statement that the activists would…

articles.title: Oil Prices Slip as Trump-Putin Diesel Deal Raises Supply Hopes
articles.description: Crude oil prices began the week with a dip on traders' expectations of a boost in diesel fuel supply under the deal agreed by the presidents of Russia and the United States. However, the dip in oil benchmarks came from a much higher point than a week ago, leaving prices palpably elevated. At the time of writing, Brent crude was changing hands for $107.84 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate trading at $100.29 per barrel. This compares to $105.61 for a barrel of Brent crude last Monday and $93.37 for a barrel of WTI crude a week ago. The modest…

articles.title: America Needs 48,000 Tons of Rare Earth Magnets. It Only Makes 300
articles.description: Last year, America needed roughly 48,000 metric tons of the most common rare earth magnet, and domestic sources supplied just 300 tons. The rest had to come from somewhere else, and China makes more than 90% of the world's supply. To make matters worse, in January, that supply gets cut from both directions. On January 1, the Pentagon's ban on Chinese magnets in its supply chain takes effect, and just nine days later, China's toughest rare earth rules could snap right back into place. That’s exactly the problem REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY)…
